messages.content:
You are an evidence extraction specialist for PFAS treatment and remediation
research. Build a structured study evidence table before any narrative review
is written.

Extract one record per primary-study experiment, modeled scenario, or field
deployment that contributes usable evidence to the review task. A paper may
produce more than one record only when materially different matrices,
technologies, operating regimes, or endpoints would otherwise be conflated.

Review articles and perspectives may help identify terminology or primary
studies, but they must not be used as the source of a quantitative study
record. Never copy a review table as though it were a primary result.

For every populated source-dependent field:
- preserve the PFAS identity or class, matrix, starting concentration or
  loading, operating conditions, study scale, measured endpoint, value, unit,
  and material qualifiers when reported;
- attach only the field-level evidence locator identifiers that directly
  support that specific value or statement;
- use an empty string or empty array when the source does not report the
  information; do not infer or estimate it;
- do not turn the absence of information in the supplied packet into a study
  finding, quantitative result, or author-reported limitation unless the source
  explicitly states that absence;
- distinguish removal, separation, sorption, parent-compound loss,
  transformation, degradation, destruction, defluorination, mineralization,
  total organofluorine change, and toxicity change;
- classify endpoint_type from what was actually measured, not from the
  authors' preferred label. Parent loss alone is not destruction. Phase
  transfer is removal or separation, not degradation. Inorganic fluoride
  release or fluorine-balance closure can establish defluorination but cannot
  by itself establish mineralization. Use mineralization only when direct
  carbon-fate evidence such as CO2/inorganic-carbon production or a carbon
  balance is reported. Preserve a broader author term in reported_term and
  explain any mismatch in interpretation;
- do not normalize or compare values unless their units, denominators,
  matrices, PFAS scope, operating conditions, and endpoints permit it.

Only populate quantitative_findings when the source reports an actual numeric
value, inequality, approximate value, range, or explicit ND/not-detected
result. Put the number or censoring marker in value and the measurement unit in
unit. Normalize Unicode inequality signs to ASCII >= or <= and range dashes to
an ASCII hyphen while preserving the source wording in qualifiers. A unit or
order-of-magnitude scale without a number is not a quantitative finding.
Qualitative parent loss, intermediate formation, or disappearance belongs in
the endpoint interpretation or residual/byproduct statements instead.

Set value_form to exactly one of:
- exact_numeric: a bare number such as `99.7` or `1.2e-3`;
- approximate_numeric: `~` followed by a number;
- inequality: `<`, `<=`, `>`, or `>=` followed by a number;
- range: two numbers separated by `-` or `to`; or
- not_detected: exactly `ND`, `N/D`, `not detected`,
  `below detection limit`, or `below quantification limit`.

Put uncertainty, denominators, fold-change wording, and explanatory text in
qualifiers rather than value. A deterministic validator will remove malformed
quantitative fields before source verification.

For limitations, use basis=author_reported only when the source states the
limitation. Use basis=design_inferred only for a constraint that follows
directly from cited design evidence, such as one matrix, one compound, or
bench-scale operation. Never label missing information in the supplied packet
as a scientific limitation of the study.

Mark each record as comparable with conditions, descriptive only, or not
comparable. Comparability is an analyst inference rather than a quotation:
attach locators for the matrix, scale, conditions, endpoint, and denominator
on which the inference rests, and explain the reason. Do not reward a study
for reporting a larger percentage when its endpoint or conditions differ.

The task was derived from a defining review that is held out from all
candidate retrieval systems. The supplied anchor identifiers are an exclusion
list, not evidence. Do not extract from the anchor, cite it, reconstruct its
conclusions, or use its tables.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied evidence-table schema exactly.
Do not write the narrative review in this step.

records.citation: Liu CJ, McKay G, Jiang D, Tenorio R, Cath JT, Amador C, Murray CC, Brown JB, Wright HB, Schaefer C, Higgins CP, Bellona C, Strathmann TJ. Pilot-scale field demonstration of a hybrid nanofiltration and UV-sulfite treatment train for groundwater contaminated by per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs). Water Res. 2021;205:117677.

comparability.reason: Rejection data are reported for a defined groundwater matrix at 90% recovery over a 30-day pilot trial. While pressure and membrane material are not reported, the clearly defined recovery and field operation make these data conditionally comparable to other NF pilot studies in similar groundwater matrices, provided differences in matrix, PFAS mixture, and recovery are accounted for.

endpoints.interpretation: NF removed PFAS from groundwater by rejecting them to the concentrate; for most detected PFAS, rejection was consistently high (>=95%) at 90% recovery, but rejection of short-chain PFSAs decreased when recovery increased from 90 to 97%.
High PFAS rejection by NF attributed to electrostatic repulsion between negatively charged membrane polymers at groundwater pH ~7.3 and size exclusion of anionic PFAS species.

limitations.statement: NF module characteristics (membrane material, manufacturer, surface charge, nominal MWCO) and operating pressure are not fully specified in the excerpt, limiting transferability of permeability and energy estimates.
Results are specific to AFFF-impacted groundwater with 12 detected PFAS and may not represent other PFAS mixtures or matrices (e.g., municipal wastewater, surface water).

Pilot-scale field demonstration of a hybrid nanofiltration and UV-sulfite treatment train for groundwater contaminated by per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs). Water Res. 2021;205:117677.

comparability.reason: NF and RO were operated at identical permeate flux (18.8 LMH) and reject flow (6.2 L/min), with the same groundwater matrix and spiked PFAS, enabling direct comparison of PFAS rejection versus recovery between the two membrane types. Comparisons to other studies still require accounting for differences in PFAS mixture, recovery range, and feed water chemistry.

endpoints.interpretation: NF rejection of PFAS decreased for short-chain PFSAs as permeate recovery increased from 90 to 97%, illustrating a tradeoff between recovery and PFAS removal performance.
RO showed superior PFAS rejection compared to NF under matched hydraulic conditions, with rejection >99% for five tested PFAS at all recoveries.
High PFAS rejection by both NF and RO attributed to electrostatic repulsion from negatively charged membrane polymers and size exclusion of anionic PFAS at groundwater pH ~7.3.

limitations.statement: Exact NF and RO membrane types, materials, and operating pressures are not provided in the excerpt, limiting interpretation of permeability and energy use.
The recovery-dependent rejection data are specific to AFFF-impacted groundwater and a limited set of PFAS (primarily PFHxA, PFOA, PFBS, PFHxS, PFOS); behavior for other PFAS or matrices may differ.

operating_conditions.name: reject_flow_rate
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Both NF and RO operated at 6.2 L/min reject flow for direct comparison.

operating_conditions.name: PFAS_spike_concentration
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Five PFAS (PFHxA, PFOA, PFBS, PFHxS, PFOS) each spiked at 0.5 µg/L into groundwater for RO rejection experiments.

operating_conditions.name: recovery_range
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Rejection of short-chain PFSAs by NF decreased when recovery increased from 90 to 97%; RO rejection of the spiked PFAS exceeded 99% at all tested recoveries (exact recoveries not otherwise specified in excerpt).

pfas_scope.value: PFHxA, PFOA, PFBS, PFHxS, PFOS each spiked at 0.5 µg/L into groundwater for RO experiments; same PFAS considered for NF vs RO rejection comparison.

quantitative_findings.name: RO rejection of PFHxA, PFOA, PFBS, PFHxS, PFOS
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: When each PFAS was spiked at 0.5 µg/L into groundwater, RO rejection exceeded 99% at all tested recoveries, under 18.8 LMH flux and 6.2 L/min reject flow.

residuals_byproducts.statement: NF and RO primarily act as separation processes concentrating PFAS in the reject stream; no PFAS destruction was reported for these membrane steps in the excerpt.

study_scale.value: Pilot-associated NF and RO recovery-dependent rejection experiments under controlled hydraulic conditions

treatment.value: Comparison of nanofiltration (NF) and reverse osmosis (RO) membranes operated at matched flux and reject flow to assess PFAS rejection as a function of water recovery.

records.citation: Liu CJ, McKay G, Jiang D, Tenorio R, Cath JT, Amador C, Murray CC, Brown JB, Wright HB, Schaefer C, Higgins CP, Bellona C, Strathmann TJ. Pilot-scale field demonstration of a hybrid nanofiltration and UV-sulfite treatment train for groundwater contaminated by per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs). Water Res. 2021;205:117677.

comparability.reason: UV-sulfite treatment conditions (10 mM sulfite, pH 11.2, up to 8 h irradiation) and reported EE/O values are specific to this pilot system and NF reject composition. Differences in reactor design, lamp type, and NF concentrate composition in other studies limit direct quantitative comparison, so these data are best used qualitatively for benchmarking.

endpoints.interpretation: The UV-sulfite process decreased PFAS parent mass in the NF reject, with >75% mass destroyed after 4 h and >90% after 8 h, based on measured PFAS concentrations. Parent loss was interpreted as PFAS destruction, although formation of transformation products is not detailed in the excerpt.

Energy per order values were calculated for removal of PFCAs and PFOS, and were relatively low (<=13.1–14.1 kWh/m3), whereas some short-chain PFSAs required >100 kWh/m3 for equivalent removal, indicating more energy-intensive treatment for short-chain sulfonates.
endpoints.reported_term: energy per order (EE/O) for PFAS removal

limitations.statement: The excerpt does not provide direct measurements of inorganic fluoride or total organofluorine, so the extent of defluorination and mineralization cannot be confirmed.
EE/O values include contributions from both UV reactor and associated systems; membrane-only energy contributions are not isolated, limiting attribution within the treatment train.

matrix.value: NF reject (10% of feed volume) from AFFF-impacted groundwater

operating_conditions.name: sulfite_concentration
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Sulfite amended to NF reject at 10 mM for UV treatment.

operating_conditions.name: pH
operating_conditions.qualifiers: UV reactor operated at pH 11.2 during sulfite treatment.

operating_conditions.name: treatment_time
operating_conditions.qualifiers: NF reject treated in UV reactor for up to 8 h; PFAS destruction evaluated at 4 and 8 h.

pfas_scope.value: PFAS present in NF reject derived from 12 PFAS detected in AFFF-impacted groundwater; results differentiated for PFCAs, PFOS, and some short-chain PFSAs.

quantitative_findings.name: PFAS mass destroyed after 4 h UV-sulfite
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: More than 75% of the detected PFAS mass in NF reject was destroyed after 4 h of UV treatment with 10 mM sulfite at pH 11.2.

quantitative_findings.name: PFAS mass destroyed after 8 h UV-sulfite
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: PFAS mass destruction increased to over 90% after 8 h UV treatment under the same conditions.

quantitative_findings.name: EE/O for PFCAs
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: Energy per order (EE/O) for PFCAs during UV-sulfite treatment was reported as <=13.1 kWh/m3.

quantitative_findings.name: EE/O for PFOS
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: Energy per order (EE/O) for PFOS was 14.1 kWh/m3.

quantitative_findings.name: EE/O for some short-chain PFSAs
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: For some short-chain PFSAs, EE/O exceeded 100 kWh/m3, indicating much higher energy demand for their removal.

residuals_byproducts.statement: While PFAS parent mass was substantially reduced (>90% after 8 h), the excerpt does not specify the identity or concentrations of transformation products or released inorganic fluoride, leaving uncertainty about byproduct formation and final fluorine speciation.

study_scale.value: Pilot-scale UV-sulfite treatment of NF reject from AFFF-impacted groundwater

treatment.value: UV-sulfite advanced reduction process treating NF reject, with sulfite amendment at alkaline pH.
